analysis.title: Stagwell Inc. (STGW): Management signals the importance of the software strategy on the Q3 results call
key_insights: Stagwell's 3Q26 call focused on its shift from a marketing services company to a technology company. Digital Transformation and Marketing Cloud were 26% of Q3 net sales and grew about 39% y/y organically.
Digital Transformation and Marketing Cloud carry higher margins than the group, at about 32% and about 44% EBITDA margin in the quarter respectively.
Enterprise tech bookings were strong. The group has delivered $59mn of software revenue YTD, with a target of $150mn next year.
Management's illustrative analysis in the investor presentation appendix assumes EBITDA from Digital Transformation and Marketing Cloud reaches $322mn by 2028 vs $88mn in 2025, a 54% CAGR.

The traditional segments (Communications, Marketing Services and Media) were broadly flat in the quarter. Illustrative EBITDA for those segments, including corporate costs, grows from $334mn in 2024 to about $392mn, a 5% CAGR.
Management remains positive on government contracts, which could grow to at least 10% of total contract value over the mid-term.
Operating cash flow was $152mn YTD, up 396% y/y.
GS expects FY26 organic growth of +7% (consensus +8.8%), with 4Q26 organic growth of +12.8%.
GS raises its Digital Transformation forecasts for FY26 and FY27 and its Marketing Cloud forecasts for FY26 and beyond.
GS FY26 adjusted EBITDA estimate is $516mn (consensus $513mn), near the midpoint of the $490-540mn guidance, with a 19.7% margin vs consensus 19.3%.
GS now expects $700mn of adjusted EBITDA by FY28, 13% above its prior forecast.
GS adjusted EPS estimates rise 3%-12% over FY26-28E. Revised FY27/FY28 EPS are 7% and 21% above consensus.
GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month target price to $14 from $13, implying about 41% upside. The stock trades on about 7x 2027E EPS vs peers on 8x.
The target price uses a DCF with WACC of 10.4% (from 9.5%, after cutting target gearing from 25% to 10%) and 2% terminal growth.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $13 to $14 on higher Digital Transformation and Marketing Cloud estimates and higher FY27-28 EBITDA. Rating reiterated, with about 41% upside to the $9.95 price.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 total pro forma net revenue was $664mn actual vs GSe $676mn and Visible Alpha consensus $681mn (reported 3Q26), up 8% y/y.
3Q26 organic growth was 7.4% actual vs GSe 8.9% and VA consensus 9.8% (reported).
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was $145mn reported vs GSe $137mn and VA consensus $137mn, up 26% y/y. Margin was 21.8% vs GSe 20.3%.
3Q26 adjusted diluted EPS was $0.34 reported vs GSe $0.33 and VA consensus $0.31, up 41% y/y from $0.24.
3Q26 Marketing Cloud revenue was $56mn reported vs GSe $24mn, with organic growth of 108.4%. Digital Transformation revenue was $119mn reported vs GSe $116mn, with organic growth of 23.1%.
3Q26 Marketing Services revenue was $218mn reported vs GSe $255mn, with organic growth of -7.5%.
GS FY26E net revenue is $2,622mn vs VA consensus $2,659mn. FY27E is $2,826mn vs $2,737mn consensus and FY28E is $3,182mn vs $2,977mn.
GS FY26E adjusted EBITDA is $516mn vs consensus $513mn. FY27E is $557mn vs $536mn and FY28E is $699mn vs $626mn.
GS adjusted diluted EPS estimates are $1.20 for FY26E (consensus $1.16), $1.38 for FY27E (consensus $1.29) and $1.92 for FY28E (consensus $1.59). 4Q26E EPS is $0.44 vs consensus $0.40.
